newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures close higher, but lack support.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures close higher, but lack support.

text.p: UK grain futures closed higher on Wednesday but traders said the market lacked firm support.

"There is no fundamental reason for the market to be higher, people say it is because there are no sellers, which there are not, but that has also been the case when the market has been coming down," said a trader.
"If someone was to come in with a big order the market would drop like a stone, but no one wants to smack it down at the moment," said another trader.
Wheat futures closed with gains of 0.55 to one stg a tonne after trading 318 lots.
Barley was 0.35 to 0.90 stg higher with 17 lots traded.
In Amsterdam the milling wheat futures market remains in the doldrums with nothing traded on Wednesday.
UK cash grain traders were also feeling sorry for themselves with little business reported in the sector.

Traders in the fob market reported a couple of runs of Jan/Mar traded at 116 and 116.50 stg a tonne ex-east coast ports while delivered business was confined to a few light loads mainly of nearby material.
